programme.title: MOTD Live: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Scotland v Brazil (Kick-off 11.00pm). Kelly Cates presents coverage of the Group C match at Miami Stadium in the USA. Brazil have been far from their imperious best so far in this tournament, but still have four points from two matches, while Scotland's win against Haiti may be enough to see them qualify, irrespective of the result here. There have been 10 previous meetings between these nations, four of which have been at the World Cup, and Scotland are still seeking a first-ever victory over the Seleção. The South Americans won three of those four World Cup clashes, the most recent of which was in the opening match of France '98 when an unlucky own-goal by Tom Boyd gave Brazil a 2-1 win, after a John Collins penalty drew Scotland level following a goal in the fifth minute by Cesar Sampaio. The last time they faced each other was a 2011 friendly at Arsenal's Emirates Stadium, when a teenage Neymar scored both goals in a 2-0 victory, at a time when he had yet to make his reputation as one the leading players in world football, two years before he moved to Barcelona from Santos

programme.title: MOTD Live: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Czechia v Mexico (Kick-off 2.00am). Coverage of the Group A match at Mexico City Stadium. The Mexicans were undefeated in the six matches they played here when hosting the 1970 and 1986 World Cups, and have continued in the same vein this time around, with a victory over South Africa here, before another win in Zapopan against South Korea ensured they were the first team to secure a place in the round of 32 and top spot in the group. In contrast, the Czechs have disappointed so far, collecting just one point against the South Africans, but a win would almost certainly send them through, either in second or as one of the best third-place teams

programme.title: MOTD Live: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Ecuador v Germany (Kick-off 9.00pm). Kelly Cates presents coverage of the Group E match at New York/New Jersey Stadium in the USA. Germany have already won the group, thanks to an injury-time winner against Ivory Coast that made it two wins from two for them, while Ecuador realistically need a win to qualify for the knockout stages. This will be the third overall meeting between these nations, and their second as part of a group stage at a World Cup after previously being drawn alongside each other at the 2006 tournament in Germany. Die Mannschaft were 3-0 winners on that occasion courtesy of a brace from Miroslav Klose and one from Lukas Podolski, which was also the final clash of the group stage, and resulted in both teams progressing to the knockout stage with Germany topping the table and La Tricolor finishing second. Tunisia have only pride to play for after suffering two heavy defeats against Sweden and Japan, while the Netherlands come into this match on the back of a 5-1 win against the Swedes. This is the first-ever competitive match between these nations, with all three previous encounters in 1978, 1994 and 2009 being friendly matches. The Eagles of Carthage will attempt to progress beyond the group stage for the first time in their history, having failed to do so at all six of their previous World Cup appearances, while Oranje will hope to continue their streak of always progressing to the knockout phase whenever a group stage has been part of the format. The Dutch are playing under the tutelage of Ronald Koeman, who is currently enjoying his second spell in charge of the national team after also having starred for them as a player, winning 78 caps and featuring at the 1990 and 1994 World Cups, the latter of which took place in the USA. programme.desc: Morocco v Haiti (Kick-off 11.00pm). Coverage of the Group C match at Atlanta Stadium in the USA. Morocco have impressed so far, drawing with Brazil and beating Scotland, while Haiti have only pride to play for having already been eliminated. Not only is this the first-ever meeting between these nations, but it is also the first competitive game against a Caribbean team for Morocco, and a maiden competitive contest for Haiti against African opposition. By qualifying for this tournament, Haiti became the first Caribbean nation to qualify for a second time after first appearing in 1974, and while they are one of two nations from the region at this tournament, alongside Curaçao, there have only been five total Caribbean teams to compete at a World Cup, the last being Trinidad & Tobago in 2006. Morocco are one of nine African teams at this year's event, which is only the second time there have been more than five countries from the continent at any one tournament, with the previous record being six competitors at the 2010 World Cup, which was held in South Africa

programme.desc: Curaçao v Ivory Coast (Kick-off 9.00pm). Coverage of the Group E match at Philadelphia Stadium in the USA. A point would be enough to see Ivory Coast through as group runners-up, while their opponents will be on a high after picking up an unexpected point against Ecuador last time out. With no World Cup experience to speak of, Curaçao will rely heavily on their Dutch coach Dick Advocaat, who has enjoyed an extensive career in both club and international football, the latter including three spells in charge of the Netherlands, in addition to roles at the helm of the UAE, South Korea, Belgium, Russia, Serbia and Iraq. This will be his second tournament in the dugout for The Blue Wave having led them at the 2025 CONCACAF Gold Cup when they failed to progress beyond the group stage after drawing with El Salvador and Canada, before losing to Honduras. Ivory Coast are managed by Emerse Faé, who earned 41 caps as a player after initially having represented his native France at under-21 level, and was appointed to this job midway through the 2023 Africa Cup of Nations after stepping up from his role in charge of the under-23s, upon which he led them to win the tournament

programme.title: MOTD Live: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Japan v Sweden (Kick-off 12.00am). Coverage of the Group F match at Dallas Stadium in the USA. This is one of the tightest groups of the tournament, with Japan undefeated after a draw against the Netherlands and a win against Tunisia, while Sweden know that a point should be enough to see them progress to the last 31, despite a heavy defeat to the Dutch last time out. At their seven previous appearances at the finals Japan have progressed to the knockout stage four times, including at the two previous tournaments in 2018 and 2022. While they finished strongly four years ago with a 2-1 win over Spain that saw them top the table, a 1-0 loss to Poland in Volgograd eight years ago meant they had to rely on Senegal also losing in their clash against Colombia and also becoming the first nation to benefit from the fair play rule to break a tied record with the unfortunate Africans. In another memorable first, Japan became the first Asian country to compete at an international tournament when they appeared in the football competition at the 1936 Olympics in Berlin, and on that occasion, they claimed a 3-2 victory over Sweden, which was seen as a massive shock at the time

programme.desc: On the beat with the police officers of Brighton after dark. Sophie and Rachel investigate a possible street assault that has left a man with life-threatening injuries and Steve comes across a pair of legs sticking out of the bushes. The question is - whose are they?

programme.title: Poisoned: Killer in the Post
programme.desc: First in a two-part documentary about The Times journalist James Beal's investigation into a disturbing number of young people dying by suicide across the UK, US, Canada, Germany and Australia, which was sparked by the death of a young man, Tom Parfett, who died by ingesting a lethal poison he had bought online. It led James to partner with bereaved parents across the globe to uncover the identity of an online poison seller, who has since been arrested and accused of sending over 1,000 packages of poison to young people

programme.title: The Accused: Beyond Reasonable Doubt?
programme.desc: Following individuals fighting convictions that they believe to be a miscarriage of justice. At a time when the British justice system is under scrutiny, this documentary explores how difficult it is to overturn a guilty verdict, revealing the emotional toll, legal hurdles and determination required to prove innocence. Beginning with a look at the case of Jason Moore, who was found guilty of murder in 2005 after a man was killed during a street fight he was involved in. Jason's family and close friends have fought tirelessly to campaign for his innocence and even enrolled an unlikely supporter: the victim's brother. When new evidence emerges, casting doubt on the eye-witness account, is it the key to freeing Jason?

programme.title: Murdered: The Baby on the Beach
programme.desc: How the discovery of a five-day-old boy's body on a lonely Co Kerry beach in April 1984 set in train a chain of events that would bring shame on the-then conservatively minded Irish state and the Gardai. An innocent woman was accused of murdering her child, leading to a tribunal now recognised as a witch hunt

programme.title: Murdered: The Baby on the Beach
programme.desc: The prosecutor makes a crucial decision to drop the charges against Joanne Hayes and the family. Questions are now asked about the validity of the Hayes' confessions, and the Kerry Babies Tribunal is established to examine the methods used by the Gardai. However, it becomes evident that the tribunal's focus is not on scrutinising the Gardai's actions but on destroying Joanne Hayes' reputation

programme.title: Murdered: The Baby on the Beach
programme.desc: Lessons to be learned from the Kerry Babies case of 1984, which shone an uncomfortable spotlight on the treatment of vulnerable women in Irish society against a backdrop of church control, police corruption and heated national debates on abortion, contraception and divorce

programme.title: George Clarke's Adventures in Americana
programme.desc: George continues his Americana odyssey in California, home of classic muscle cars, the double decker burger, and a skyscraper built on its side in the middle of the desert. programme.desc: In 2009, 17-year-old Stacey Hyde was arrested for killing her best friend's boyfriend. She stabbed him to death after a drunken fight in his flat. Stacey insisted she was defending herself and her friend. But as her criminal charge reached court, the jury saw differently and found her guilty of murder. Those close to Stacey stood by her and searched for a way to prove that she acted in self-defence. Could the charity Justice for Women offer a way out? Stacey Hyde's case is one of many in which women who kill are imprisoned for murder, even though the courts may not have fully examined the circumstances that led to the event

programme.title: Murdered: The Baby on the Beach

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 26 Live
programme.desc: Switzerland v Canada (Kick-off 8.00pm). Joanne Cantwell presents coverage of both teams' concluding Group B match, held at BC Place Vancouver in Canada. The only previous meeting between these nations was a friendly match in 2002 that took place on Swiss soil, and saw the Canadians claim a 3-1 victory. This time around, both teams look all but certain to advance to the last 32 after each taking four points from their matches against Bosnia and Herzegovina and Qatar, with the co-hosts just needing a draw to guarantee top spot due to their superior goal difference. With analysis from Kevin Doyle

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 26 Live
programme.desc: Scotland v Brazil (Kick-off 11.00pm). Joanne Cantwell presents coverage of the Group C match at Miami Stadium in the USA. Brazil have been far from their imperious best so far in this tournament, but still have four points from two matches, while Scotland's win against Haiti may be enough to see them qualify, irrespective of the result here. There have been 10 previous meetings between these nations, four of which have been at the World Cup, and Scotland are still seeking a first-ever victory over the Seleção. The South Americans won three of those four World Cup clashes, the most recent of which was in the opening match of France '98 when an unlucky own-goal by Tom Boyd gave Brazil a 2-1 win, after a John Collins penalty drew Scotland level following a goal in the fifth minute by Cesar Sampaio. The last time they faced each other was a 2011 friendly at Arsenal's Emirates Stadium, when a teenage Neymar scored both goals in a 2-0 victory, at a time when he had yet to make his reputation as one the leading players in world football, two years before he moved to Barcelona from Santos

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 26 Live
programme.desc: Curaçao v Ivory Coast (Kick-off 9.00pm). Coverage of the Group E match at Philadelphia Stadium in the USA. A point would be enough to see Ivory Coast through as group runners-up, while their opponents will be on a high after picking up an unexpected point against Ecuador last time out. With no World Cup experience to speak of, Curaçao will rely heavily on their Dutch coach Dick Advocaat, who has enjoyed an extensive career in both club and international football, the latter including three spells in charge of the Netherlands, in addition to roles at the helm of the UAE, South Korea, Belgium, Russia, Serbia and Iraq. This will be his second tournament in the dugout for The Blue Wave having led them at the 2025 CONCACAF Gold Cup when they failed to progress beyond the group stage after drawing with El Salvador and Canada, before losing to Honduras. Ivory Coast are managed by Emerse Faé, who earned 41 caps as a player after initially having represented his native France at under-21 level, and was appointed to this job midway through the 2023 Africa Cup of Nations after stepping up from his role in charge of the under-23s, upon which he led them to win the tournament

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 26 Live
programme.desc: Colombia v DR Congo (Kick-off 3.00am). All the action from both teams' second match in Group K, held at Guadalajara Stadium in Mexico. The Colombians have reached the knockout stage on three of the six occasions they have qualified for the finals, including the most recent appearance in 2018. Having faced Uzbekistan in their opening group contest, they will be looking to secure a place in the last 32 here before a final-game showdown with Portugal. However, they can take nothing for granted against the talented African outfit who are looking to make an impact in their first finals since 1974, when the country was known as Zaire. Colombia made a good start to their campaign on Wednesday with a 3-1 victory against Uzbekistan, while DR Congo played out an impressive 1-1 draw against Portugal

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 26 Live
programme.desc: Curaçao v Ivory Coast (Kick-off 9.00pm). Coverage of the Group E match at Philadelphia Stadium in the USA. A point would be enough to see Ivory Coast through as group runners-up, while their opponents will be on a high after picking up an unexpected point against Ecuador last time out. With no World Cup experience to speak of, Curaçao will rely heavily on their Dutch coach Dick Advocaat, who has enjoyed an extensive career in both club and international football, the latter including three spells in charge of the Netherlands, in addition to roles at the helm of the UAE, South Korea, Belgium, Russia, Serbia and Iraq. This will be his second tournament in the dugout for The Blue Wave having led them at the 2025 CONCACAF Gold Cup when they failed to progress beyond the group stage after drawing with El Salvador and Canada, before losing to Honduras. Ivory Coast are managed by Emerse Faé, who earned 41 caps as a player after initially having represented his native France at under-21 level, and was appointed to this job midway through the 2023 Africa Cup of Nations after stepping up from his role in charge of the under-23s, upon which he led them to win the tournament

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 26 Live
programme.desc: Cape Verde v Saudi Arabia (Kick-off 1.00am). All the action from both teams' third and final Group H match, held at Houston Stadium in the USA. Uruguay and Spain were the two favourites to qualify from this group, but even if both of these sides have failed to collect a point so far, with eight of the 12 third-placed teams qualifying for the last 32, three points here could be enough to see either one of them progress. The only time the Saudis managed to reach the knockout stage was in 1994, when the United States served as hosts, while this is the first time Cape Verde have played in the finals. Both of these sides still have a chance of progressing to the knock-out stages and a victory here may well do the job. Cape Verde are currently third in the group with two points, while Saudi Arabia are bottom with one, but the result in the other game between Spain and Uruguay may affect what happens to these teams

programme.desc: Paraguay v Australia (Kick-off 3.00am). Coverage of the Group D match at San Francisco Bay Area Stadium in Santa Clara, USA. Co-hosts USA have already won this group, having beaten both of these two, and the runners-up will go on to meet the second-placed team in Group G. This will be the first-ever competitive fixture between these nations, with all five of the previous meetings being friendly matches. The South Americans are yet to taste victory against the Socceroos, who have won two of the five contests, including the most recent encounter in Sydney in October 2010. Both nations produced their best-ever World Cup performance when they last appeared at the finals, with Los Guaraníes reaching the quarter-finals in South Africa in 2010 and Australia making it to the last 16 for the second time four years ago in Qatar, in a tournament that saw them register more than one victory for the first time

It's an idyllic location, but their home is also their workplace and it's starting to feel a bit cramped. The couple want to stay put in their exclusive location, so Linda has hatched an ambitious plan to buy the boat next door and do it up all by herself. It's a huge challenge and it remains to be seen whether enthusiasm and passion will be enough to get the job done

programme.title: Love Your Garden
programme.desc: Alan Titchmarsh and the team of horticultural experts meet wheelchair user Rhyanne Nixon, whose bare garden is dominated by a large wooden viewing platform that she cannot access. As a former holistic practitioner, she wants a vibrant outdoor space filled with different colours and smells, and hopes a new pond and flowers will attract a variety of wildlife to the area

programme.title: My Greek Kitchen
programme.desc: Part two of two. Tonia Buxton goes on a fishing trip with her father in a bid to catch local octopus, which she combines with red wine to make stew

programme.title: My Greek Kitchen
programme.desc: Tonia Buxton travels to Athens, where she rustles up Avgolemono soup - a filling chicken and rice recipe - and souvlaki, one of the Greeks' favourite fast-food dishes

programme.title: Country House Auction
programme.desc: Newlywed couple Tessa and Robin juggle running a 48-bedroom castle and 50 acres of land with a special pair of Royal Highlander cows. In the auction room, a small but perfectly formed painting by one of the world's most famous artists, John Constable, is ready for auction. Silver enthusiast Oliver desperately hopes that a late 19th-century Japanese silver punchbowl will be coming home with him, while auctioneer Michael needs to sell a 1930s Philco radio that props-buyer Bridie and her mother Sara have fallen in love with

programme.title: My Floating Home

programme.title: Love Your Garden
programme.desc: Kent couple Lou and Andy Webb have two young children affected by a rare genetic condition that severely restricts their eyesight, meaning they only see in black and white and have to wear special goggles in sunlight. Alan Titchmarsh's challenge is to create a more child-friendly garden for their terraced home in Tonbridge, and his first task is to make a shady environment so the kids can spend time outside in the day. After that, he and the team come up with a bespoke lighting system for the evenings, acoustic fencing to cut down the noise from a nearby railway line, and an area for the parents

programme.title: Yorkshire by the Sea
programme.desc: Fisherman Darren heads into the North Sea from Staithes in search of lobster and crab. Shellfish are now a mainstay of the catch on the Yorkshire coast, with conservationists ensuring that the lobster population remains buoyant by breeding and releasing them from a purpose-built hatchery in Whitby. Plus, a new recruit joins the team running the historic tramway in Saltburn, and an ambitious couple launch the first wine grown in their Robin Hood's Bay vineyard

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Originally from India, Bindu grew up with a garden full of vegetables, nature and birdsong and would like to recreate a bit of that in her modest garden in Warrington, Cheshire. The garden is a sun trap, so she and partner Vivek want some height and shade in the plot as well as raised beds for fruit and veg growing. It's very important to them that they try and care for the environment too so would like the means to harvest rainwater and compost waste. With a relatively small budget of £3,000, Charlie Dimmock and Lee Hull create a garden that is both eco-friendly and looks beautiful

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Charlie Dimmock and Flo Headlam come up with plans to transform a characterless garden in Daventry into a curvy, naturalistic oasis with a spiritual, Dartmoor-inspired atmosphere

programme.title: Permissive (1970)
programme.desc: A woman comes to London to visit an old friend, and gets drawn into the world of rock band groupies. She quickly sinks into a self-destructive hedonistic lifestyle, and is consumed with jealousy as she and rival groupies bitterly compete to outshine each other in the eyes of the musicians they cling to. Drama, starring Maggie Stride and Gay Singleton

programme.title: The Playbirds (1978)
programme.desc: An elusive killer is murdering women who have posed for a porn magazine, so a female detective is given the task of going undercover as a nude model to lure him into a trap. Drama, starring Mary Millington and Glynn Edwards

programme.title: The Blood on Satan's Claw (1971)
programme.desc: Strange remains are discovered in a 17th-century farming village, and have a disturbing effect on the townsfolk. They form a sinister cult, performing strange and violent rituals to bring their demonic master back to life. However, a pious judge is prepared to use brutal methods of his own to root out the evil. Horror, starring Patrick Wymark, Linda Hayden and Simon Williams
